name: Downtown and Church Street
tagline: The pedestrian marketplace and the lakefront below it
description: The centre of the city around the Church Street Marketplace, four blocks closed to traffic and genuinely busy, with the restaurants, the bars, the coworking and the walk down to the lakefront path. Almost everything Burlington offers is within ten minutes of here.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to live without a car
pros: A real pedestrian centre, not a token block
Lakefront and bike path below it
All the coworking and most of the food
cons: The most expensive rents in the city
Very hard to find anything available
Busy and loud around the marketplace

name: Old North End
tagline: The dense, diverse and cheapest part of the city
description: The neighbourhood north of downtown, the densest in Vermont and the most diverse, with resettled communities from Bosnia, Somalia, Nepal and Congo, small groceries reflecting all of them, and the city's most affordable housing.
bestFor: Budget stays within walking distance of downtown
cons: Older housing stock, often poorly insulated
Higher crime rates than the rest of the city

name: South End
tagline: The arts district in the old industrial buildings
description: The area south of downtown along Pine Street, where former factories now hold studios, breweries, design offices and the South End Art Hop each September. The bike path runs along the lake at its western edge and Oakledge Park is at the end of it.
bestFor: Anyone wanting studio space, breweries and the bike path
pros: The city's arts and maker cluster
Bike path and Oakledge Park nearby
cons: Not walkable to downtown, twenty minutes on foot

name: Winooski
tagline: The mill city across the river, cheaper and lively
description: A separate small city just across the Winooski River, built around the old woollen mills and now holding a compact roundabout centre with a surprisingly good restaurant and bar scene. Rents are below Burlington and the bike ride into downtown takes fifteen minutes.
bestFor: Anyone wanting Burlington access at lower rents
pros: Genuinely good food for its size
Fifteen minutes to downtown by bike
cons: The roundabout traffic is a local joke
Bus service is limited in the evening

name: South Burlington
tagline: The suburban side with the airport and the shops
description: The town immediately south and east, holding the airport, the shopping centres and most of the region's newer apartment complexes. It is car-dependent and unremarkable, and it is where availability actually exists when downtown has nothing.
bestFor: Anyone who needs newer housing and can drive
pros: Newer apartment stock and actual availability
cons: Ten to fifteen minutes from downtown
